findings.description: On refill, `bucket.tokens` is increased, but `bucket.updated_at` is only advanced on the allowed path. When a request is denied (line 71 returns early), the refilled tokens are kept while `updated_at` stays old. The next call computes `elapsed` from the old timestamp and adds the same interval's refill again. Example: capacity 10, rate 1/s, tokens 0 at t=0. A cost-10 request denied at t=5 leaves tokens=5 and updated_at=0. At t=6 elapsed=6, so tokens become 11 and are capped to 10, when only 6 should be available. Clients that keep retrying while limited therefore get more throughput than the configured rate.
findings.suggestion: Set `bucket.updated_at = now` immediately after the refill on line 69, before the `bucket.tokens < cost` check, so it advances on both the allowed and denied paths.
findings.title: Denied requests double-count token refill
